In an open letter titled “A Warning Against Contracting with Duplicity,” Ike Boss, a communications practitioner and founding fellow of The Boss Group (TBG), issues a stern warning to all political parties involved in Johannesburg’s coalition negotiations.

Describing the situation as one where “the architecture of bad faith” sits across the negotiating table, Boss raises serious concerns about Helen Zille and the DA’s record on accountability, leadership, power-sharing and the ability to honour coalition agreements.

The letter challenges political parties to look beyond promises of good governance and assess the DA on its actions and track record.
Johannesburg’s future cannot be held hostage by political egos, backroom manoeuvring and broken promises. Residents deserve a coalition built on accountability, mutual respect and service delivery.

🎂🤱 FROM GA-RAMOTSE TO 67 YEARS OF PURPOSE

Today, 67 years ago, on the 26th of August 1959, a little boy was born in a small rural village called Ga-Ramotse in Hammanskraal.

A young boy who lost his father at the age of two, and whose mother was forced to leave home to work as a domestic worker in what was once known as the City of Gold, Jozi Maboneng. She did not leave because she wanted to; poverty gave her no choice. Her sacrifice meant that his sisters had to help raise him, while his grandfather, who named him High Man at birth, taught him lessons that would shape his life: that life demands resilience, responsibility and determination.

That little boy never allowed the circumstances of his childhood to define the limits of his future. He understood that his mother's absence was not abandonment, but an act of love and sacrifice, a mother doing whatever she could to put food on the table and give her children a chance at a better life. From his sisters, he learnt strength; from his grandfather, he inherited resilience, hard work and determination; and from Ga-Ramotse, he learnt never to forget where he came from. Those early lessons became the foundation of the man he has now become.

That little boy was me, Herman Philip Samtseu Mashaba.

Today, as I turn 67, I look back with gratitude at the journey from that small village to becoming a successful entrepreneur, a leader and a servant of my country, the accidental Mayor that has always been seen as the outsider, for serving in the intrest of those he leads. Today, I carry my father's memory, my mother's sacrifice, my sisters' strength and my grandfather's voice with me every day.

My journey has never been about escaping where I come from; it has been about using where I come from as the strength to fight for a better future for those who still live with the circumstances I once knew.

I have come a long way, but the fight to change the narrative of our people continues.

Happy Birthday to myself. 🎂

@hermanspmashaba is a South African politician, entrepreneur and the current President of ActionSA, a business leader turned public figure whose journey reflects the power of entrepreneurship as a pathway to influence and national impact. From building one of South Africa’s most successful indigenous consumer brands to leading one of its largest cities as Mayor of Johannesburg, Herman Mashaba has consistently positioned enterprise, accountability, and economic inclusion at the center of his work.
